catalog_quote: Stress in Ormuri is dynamic, non-mobile, and may fall on any syllable in the word, as is shown in disyllabic words where it may be on either syllable, and in tri- and quadri-syllables (of which there are considerably fewer) where it is on the second, third or fourth syllable from the beginning of the word. ... As regards its position in the word, stress in Ormuri is non-mobile; that is to say, it falls on a specific syllable. The only exceptions are the finite forms of the present and aorist tenses of the 2nd and 4th conjugations, where it regularly moves from the ending onto the root in the 2sg. forms (see section 3.2). ... We paid particular attention to word stress when collecting and analysing the material on Logar and Kaniguram. Our material confirms that Meillet and Gauthiot‘s hypothesis is of doubtful applicability to stress in Ormuri. Stress in the modern language is truly dynam…

audit.deciding_source_year: 2011 (English translation of the 1986 Russian monograph; fieldwork Logar 1971 + Kaniguram material)
audit.reasoning: (1) The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Efimov 2011 text at sec. 2.6, pp. 88-90, exactly as located; elisions are marked and skip only example lists and footnotes. (2) The classification rests on the standard modern reference grammar (Efimov 1986/2011, fieldwork-based, both dialects, stress a declared focus), which explicitly says stress is dynamic, fixed per word, may fall on any syllable and 'does not depend on quantitative factors'; the earlier weight-sensitive screen came from Morgenstierne 1929 sec. 42, which I re-checked in the held text and which is a reconstruction of the ancestor dialect, not a synchronic rule. (3) An open independent source fetched sources now (Trofimov 2022, JoLR 20) quotes the same Efimov characterization ('raznomestnoe, nepodvizhnoe, silovoe') and builds a lexical barytone/oxytone analysis on it -- confirms LEXICAL. No instrumental study or JIPA Illustrat

sources.citation: Trofimov, Artem A. 2022. Udarenie v jazykax parachi i ormuri v svjazi s afganskim i ego znachenie dlja iranskoj rekonstrukcii [The accent in Parachi and Ormuri compared to Pashto and its significance for the reconstruction of Proto-Iranian]. Journal of Language Relationship / Voprosy jazykovogo rodstva 20(3-4): 222-252. DOI 10.31826/jlr-2023-203-407.
sources.quote: Quotes Efimov 1985:35 / 1986:107-108 as the standard description: 'Ударение в ормури разноместное, неподвижное, силовое. Разноместный (или свободный) характер ударения в именах и глаголах проявляется в том, что в двусложных словах оно может находиться на любом слоге, в трех- и четырехсложных ... на втором, третьем или четвертом слоге от начала' (stress in Ormuri is free-position [raznomestnoe], non-mobile, dynamic; in disyllables on either syllable, in tri/quadrisyllables on 2nd, 3rd or 4th). The article then treats Ormuri nominal/verbal stems as lexically barytone vs oxytone, matching Pashto
sources.note: Only recent dedicated accentological study of Ormuri; independently restates Efimov's 'free, non-mobile, dynamic' characterization and analyses stems as lexical barytone/oxytone classes -- a second, independent citation for the LEXICAL coding.
